properties.name: Cagayan River Basin
properties.description: The largest river basin in the Philippines. Houses Magat Dam and provides irrigation for the nation's premier corn and northern rice granary. Prone to severe agricultural drought during El Niño.

properties.name: Mindanao River Basin (Cotabato)
properties.description: Second largest river basin in the country, encompassing the Ligawasan Marsh. Crucial for southern agricultural production; severe dry spells trigger widespread crop failures and river low-flow.

properties.name: Agusan River Basin
properties.description: Third largest river basin, including the Agusan Marsh wildlife sanctuary. Influenced heavily by Pacific climate patterns; experiences reduced wetland replenishment during ENSO events.

properties.name: Pampanga River Basin
properties.description: The economic and agricultural backbone of Central Luzon. Fed by Pantabangan Dam and Angat Dam; supplies water to both Central Luzon agriculture and Metro Manila.

properties.name: Agno River Basin
properties.description: Drains from the Cordillera mountains to the Lingayen Gulf. Cascaded by Ambuklao, Binga, and San Roque dams for 680 MW hydroelectric generation and extensive Pangasinan irrigation.

properties.name: Abra River Basin
properties.description: Sixth largest river basin, draining the central Cordillera into the West Philippine Sea. Experiences sharp drop in base flow during prolonged dry seasons.

properties.name: Pasig-Marikina-Laguna de Bay Basin
properties.description: The most densely populated river basin in the Philippines. Houses La Mesa Dam and Laguna Lake, directly sustaining water security for over 16 million residents.

properties.name: Bicol River Basin
properties.description: Extends from Albay through Lake Bato and Lake Buhi to San Miguel Bay. Principal rice production zone of Region V, highly susceptible to rainfall anomaly swings.

properties.name: Apayao-Abulug River Basin
properties.description: Drains the northernmost Cordillera ranges into the Babuyan Channel; crucial pristine watershed for northern Luzon.

properties.name: Tagum-Libuganon River Basin
properties.description: Heart of Davao Region's high-value commercial banana and coconut export plantations; vulnerable to prolonged soil moisture deficits.

properties.name: Ilog-Hilabangan River Basin
properties.description: Major river basin of Negros Island. Supplies vital irrigation for sugarcane plantations; severely stressed during the 2015–16 and 2023–24 El Niño droughts.

properties.name: Panay River Basin
properties.description: Spans northern Panay Island; critical for Western Visayas rice, corn, and aquaculture sectors.

properties.name: Tagoloan River Basin
properties.description: Originates in the high plateaus of Bukidnon and discharges into Macajalar Bay; major source of agricultural and industrial water.

properties.name: Agus River Basin
properties.description: The primary hydroelectric corridor of Mindanao, draining Lake Lanao over a 36-km descent through six hydropower plants (Agus 1 through 7).

properties.name: Davao River Basin
properties.description: Provides municipal, commercial, and agricultural water for the growing Davao metropolitan area.

properties.name: Cagayan de Oro River Basin
properties.description: Drains the Kalatungan and Kitanglad mountain ranges into Macajalar Bay; supplies Metro Cagayan de Oro.

properties.name: Jalaur River Basin
properties.description: Vital lifeline for Iloilo Province, supporting the newly developed Jalaur River Multipurpose Project (JRMP II) to buffer Western Visayas against seasonal droughts.

properties.name: Buayan-Malungon River Basin
properties.description: Empties into Sarangani Bay; critical watershed for General Santos City tuna cannery operations and surrounding fruit plantations.
